newsitem.title: USA: Tax caps on ballot in 20 Illinois counties.
newsitem.headline: Tax caps on ballot in 20 Illinois counties.

text.p: Voters in 20 Illinois counties will decide Nov. 5 whether they want limitations on local property tax increases, according to an unofficial accounting by the Illinois Board of Elections.

The board, which is expected to release the official tally of county tax cap elections next week, listed the counties as Boone, Champaign, Christian, Franklin, Jackson, Kankakee, Lee, Logan, Macoupin, Massac, McLean, Menard, Monroe, Morgan, Randolph, Sangamon, Schuyler, Union, Williamson and Winnebago.
Under a measure passed by the Illinois General Assembly in May, county boards in 96 counties outside of the Chicago area were able to place tax caps referendums on the ballot.

The tax caps, already in place in six Chicago area counties, limit annual increases in local property tax collections to five percent or the rate of inflation, whichever is less. The restriction also prohibits the issuance of general obligation debt without voter approval.
